prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional small molecules that recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases

statement.case_for: After the full exchange I keep B041 as a single-achievement prize, and the case rests on the same point as before: a PROTAC is a designed molecule with a recognition end, an effector end and a linker, and it converts the cell's own ubiquitin-proteasome machinery into a drug mechanism. That is event-driven, catalytic pharmacology in place of occupancy-driven inhibition, and it has been adopted by many independent groups, so it is no longer one laboratory's claim. The three names map onto separable, checkable contributions: Crews for the concept and first cell-active proof, Deshaies for the early demonstration that recruiting an E3 ligase works and for the cullin-ligase biology behind it, and Ciulli for structure-guided VHL ligands and the ternary-complex rationale that made degraders rational and drug-like. Nothing in round 1 changed that credit logic. What round 1 did change is my view of how firm the other candidates are: every one of them was shown to carry an unresolved credit or category problem, so I do not think B041 is unusual in having one, and I would not call the clinical gap disqualifying when the field has a large late-stage pipeline.
statement.case_against: The cereblon and molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray) is a genuinely separate line of discovery. The chair's attribution question is fair: a citation about heterobifunctional molecules recruiting E3 ligases leaves out the work that explains how thalidomide-type drugs act, and a citation broad enough to include it needs more than three names. No PROTAC is approved, so recognition could be a few years early, and a committee that wants an approved medicine will see this as less mature than B023 or B039. I also accept that choosing Ciulli over Handa is a judgement about which strand is the defining one, and a reasonable member could judge it the other way.

responses.point: Chabes pairs B060 (Liu) with B041 limited to Crews and Deshaies, framed as chemically induced proximity, and says the PROTAC and cereblon strands are not yet allocated.
responses.response: This is the pairing I can most readily support after B041 alone, and I would not block it. Where I differ is the framing and the third name. Chemically induced proximity is broad enough to cover glues, but it stretches a citation over work that two names cannot honestly carry, and it drops Ciulli, whose structure-guided VHL ligands turned the concept into a design discipline. I also remain unpersuaded that B060 adds a distinct chemical principle beyond the 2020 CRISPR recognition, so for me the second part costs coherence without adding a decisive achievement. I am keeping Ciulli in my configuration and treating Chabes's version as an acceptable fallback, not as my preference.

responses.point: The chair lists B060 and B041 as alternatives to his nanopore choice and asks whether the committee can agree three names for B041, noting his own opening ballot used Crews, Ciulli and Handa.
responses.response: The chair's version is the best argument for a cereblon-inclusive citation, and I take it seriously: Handa's identification of cereblon is a real discovery that explains why the glue degraders work. My answer is that it is a mechanism-of-action discovery for a drug class, whereas the PROTAC strand is a design principle that anyone can reuse with a new target and a new ligase. Those two ideas belong in one story but not in one three-name credit. If the committee insists on one citation covering both, I would accept Handa in place of Ciulli, but I would not accept dropping Deshaies. On B039 I still see the attribution as harder than B041, because the chair himself says the three-person cut omits Branton or Kasianowicz, whose 1996 experiment is the founding result.

responses.point: Somfai pairs B023 (Buchwald and Hartwig) with B060 (Liu) and asks what is chemically new in base editing, given that he regards C-N coupling as the clearest general method on the shortlist.
responses.response: I agree that B023 has the cleanest credit and the longest record, and I share his question about the chemical novelty in B060. The deamination chemistry is real and the protein-evolution step is impressive, but the programmable targeting comes from Cas9, which the 2020 prize already honoured. My concern about B023 is not quality but whether it carries enough new conceptual content, given the 2010 prize, to be this year's choice. If the committee wanted a two-part prize with a classical synthetic part, I could accept B023 as the partner for B041, which would give a molecule-making method and a new therapeutic modality, but I would prefer that to Somfai's pairing only if five members will support it.

responses.point: Sparr maintains that condensates (B052) are a new organising principle of physical chemistry, accepts the in vivo controversy and notes that Pappu and Mittag fall outside the three-name limit.
responses.response: I appreciate that she states the credit and in vivo problems herself, and I agree with her that the in vitro multivalent phase-transition work and the P-granule demonstration stand on their own. That is precisely why I keep it only in third place for this year: the founding observations are secure, but the framing of which cellular assemblies are really phase separated is still being refined, and the sequence grammar that Pappu and Mittag supplied is central rather than peripheral. A prize that cannot name them has a hole at its centre. I would revisit B052 in a later year, and I do not think we should vote for it now.

uncertainties: Whether any pairing can reach five votes: B041 with B060 and B041 with B023 are both plausible but neither has been tested, and I am unsure which one the committee would take.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes recognition premature this year.
Whether the cereblon molecular-glue strand should be in the same citation, which decides whether Ciulli or Handa is the third name.
How much weight to give the fact that I am the only member who ranked B041 first in the opening, and whether I am overvaluing the design-principle argument.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. None of the credited names on B041 is a postdoc mentor (Stevens, Boey), collaborator or Linköping colleague. I share peptide and protein self-assembly interests with Emma Sparr, which bears on B052 only as field overlap. My work on peptide-based biosensing and hydrogels is adjacent to chemical biology generally but not to any named degrader candidate. I disclose no change since round 1.
